heard: The sun and moon look identical in our sky. Most people assume they are naturally similar in size. But the sun is roughly 400 times wider than the moon. It is also 400 times farther away from Earth. That matching ratio makes both objects span half a degree. During totality, the moon covers the sun's disk completely. This perfect cosmic match grants Artemis II astronauts a 57-minute eclipse. It is the only reason they look identical in our sky.
